Patient_Actor.history: A 39-year-old woman comes to the physician because of recurrent episodes of severe pain over her neck, back, and shoulders for the past year. The pain worsens with exercise and lack of sleep. Use of over-the-counter analgesics have not resolved her symptoms. She also has stiffness of the shoulders and knees and tingling in her upper extremities that is worse in the morning. She takes escitalopram for generalized anxiety disorder. She also has tension headaches several times a month. Her maternal uncle has ankylosing spondylitis. Examination shows marked tenderness over the posterior neck, bilateral mid trapezius, and medial aspect of the left knee. Muscle strength is normal. Laboratory studies, including a complete blood count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and thyroid-stimulating hormone are within the reference ranges. X-rays of her cervical and lumbar spine show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
